nodes.description: Heterozygous missense substitutions at Arg157, Pro160 or Gln161 in a highly conserved stretch of the glutamine-rich N-terminus; Arg157 and Pro160 lie in the tankyrase-binding motif of AMOTL1. AMOTL1 tolerates loss of function (pLI 0) and Amotl1 deletion mice survive normally, while R157C knock-in mice have reduced survival, so the variants are thought to act by gain of function or dominant interference rather than haploinsufficiency. The functional category is left unset because the sources do not settle it: the mutants also lose a normal function, since R157C escapes DDI2 cleavage and so no longer promotes focal-adhesion maturation.

nodes.description: R157C AMOTL1 reduces both the speed and the directional persistence of collectively migrating cells. Overexpressed wild-type AMOTL1 also slows migration, but less, so part of the effect is one of excess AMOTL1 rather than specific to the mutant. Cell adhesion and migration underlie lip, palate and heart morphogenesis, which is the proposed link to the malformations.
